name: 20 Leonis Minoris A
description: A naked-eye star 15.0 parsecs away, 1.2 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the CHARA Array.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 86728: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.771 +/- 0.012 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 1.247 +/- 0.021

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 86728: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.034 +/- 0.036

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 86728: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5612 +/- 52

distance.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 86728: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 66.47 +/- 0.32 mas, inverted

text.card: A naked-eye star 15 parsecs away whose disc the CHARA Array measured: 1.2 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 0.771 milliarcseconds, which gives 1.247 solar radii and 5,612 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 5 and 10, HD 86728: limb-darkened diameter, R, Teff
